findings.title: AI search and retrieval crawlers blocked from root (OAI-SearchBot, Claude-SearchBot, PerplexityBot)
findings.evidence: Observed at https://launchpad.net/robots.txt via robots_txt_parser_longest_match [2026-09-13T15:53:42Z]: robots.txt disallows root '/' for retrieval agents: OAI-SearchBot, Claude-SearchBot, PerplexityBot, Claude-User. These build the indexes AI answers are assembled from, or fetch a page live when a user asks about it, so the brand cannot be cited at all. Training-only crawlers (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, Google-Extended, CCBot, Applebot-Extended, Meta-ExternalAgent, Bytespider, Amazonbot) are also blocked, which is a separate and legitimate licensing choice. (Confidence: high)

suggested_action.summary: Allow AI search and user-triggered retrieval agents, even if training crawlers stay blocked.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: In robots.txt, allow OAI-SearchBot, Claude-SearchBot and PerplexityBot (search indexes) and ChatGPT-User, Claude-User and Perplexity-User (live user fetches). You can keep GPTBot, ClaudeBot, Google-Extended and CCBot disallowed if you do not want your content used for model training -- the two decisions are independent.
suggested_action.expected_benefit: Improves crawlability by making the observed information clearer and more extractable for the intended audience.

evidence_details.observation: robots.txt disallows root '/' for retrieval agents: OAI-SearchBot, Claude-SearchBot, PerplexityBot, Claude-User. Training-only crawlers (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, Google-Extended, CCBot, Applebot-Extended, Meta-ExternalAgent, Bytespider, Amazonbot) are also blocked, which is a separate and legitimate licensing choice.

findings.severity_rationale: Rated critical because the observed evidence indicates critical impact; unavailable evidence is not treated as a defect.

findings.title: Missing viewport meta tag hampers mobile user engagement
findings.evidence:
Observed at https://launchpad.net/+login via mobile_viewport_inspector [2026-09-13T15:53:42Z]: HTML <head> lacks <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">, causing mobile browsers to render desktop scale. (Confidence: high)
Additional evidence (engagement-audit): Observed at https://launchpad.net/+tour/index via mobile_viewport_inspector [2026-09-13T15:53:42Z]: HTML <head> lacks <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">, causing mobile browsers to render desktop scale. (Confidence: high)
Additional evidence (engagement-audit): Observed at https://launchpad.net/beautifulsoup via mobile_viewport_inspector [2026-09-13T15:53:42Z]: HTML <head> lacks <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">, causing mobile browsers to render desktop scale. (Confidence: high)

suggested_action.summary: Add responsive viewport meta tag to HTML head.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Insert <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0"> into the document <head>.
suggested_action.expected_benefit: Improves orientation by making the observed information clearer and more extractable for the intended audience.

assessments.reason: robots.txt was fetched and its rules were applied to page and link fetches.
Initial HTML was inspected for shell signals; no browser rendering was used.
Answerability was checked against accessible on-site text and structured data only.
Only explicitly linked authority domains were inspected; external sources were not fabricated or searched.
No agent-supplied external discovery evidence was provided; no external search was performed.

proactive_recommendations.title: Mark up existing question-and-answer content with FAQPage schema
proactive_recommendations.rationale: The site already contains question-shaped content, but none of it is marked as FAQPage. FAQPage is the highest-leverage schema type for AI citation because its question/answer structure matches how retrieval systems chunk content and lift a quotable answer. The content already exists; only the markup is missing.

suggested_action.summary: Add FAQPage JSON-LD to pages that already answer common questions.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Wrap each question and its answer in FAQPage JSON-LD with mainEntity -> Question -> acceptedAnswer. Mark up the answers you already publish rather than writing new ones.

proactive_recommendations.title: Build third-party presence so Launchpad is resolvable away from its own domain
proactive_recommendations.rationale: Only 1 independent authority domain(s) are referenced from the crawled pages. Assistants weight facts that several unrelated sources agree on, and the major platforms draw on largely different source pools -- analyses of 2026 citation data find roughly 11% domain overlap between ChatGPT and Perplexity. A brand described only on its own site is a single fragile source no matter how well that site is built.

suggested_action.summary: Establish and maintain the brand on independent platforms, then link them via sameAs.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Create or claim a Wikidata item, a LinkedIn company page, and the profiles that matter in your sector (Crunchbase, GitHub, G2, industry registries). Keep the core facts identical across them, then reference them from Organization sameAs so the identity is machine-linkable.

proactive_recommendations.title: Add Article schema with author and dateModified to editorial pages
proactive_recommendations.rationale: 1 crawled page(s) are editorial or documentation content carrying no Article schema. Authorship and a machine-readable modification date are the signals assistants use to decide whether a passage is current and attributable -- without them, an assistant that finds a good answer on the page still has no basis to date it or credit it.

suggested_action.summary: Mark editorial and documentation pages with Article JSON-LD.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Add Article or TechArticle JSON-LD with headline, author (a Person or Organization with a real profile URL), datePublished and dateModified. Update dateModified when the content genuinely changes, not on every deploy.

proactive_recommendations.title: Declare a WebSite entity with SearchAction
proactive_recommendations.rationale: No WebSite schema was found. WebSite ties the domain to the brand entity and, with a potentialAction SearchAction, lets assistants point users straight into your own search instead of guessing at URLs. It is a small, stable addition that anchors everything else on the page to a named site.

suggested_action.summary: Add WebSite JSON-LD with a SearchAction pointing at your search endpoint.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Add WebSite JSON-LD on the homepage with name, url, a publisher reference to your Organization @id, and potentialAction -> SearchAction with a target URL template.

proactive_recommendations.title: Add BreadcrumbList schema to deep pages
proactive_recommendations.rationale: 2 crawled page(s) sit two or more levels deep with no BreadcrumbList markup. Breadcrumbs give both a visitor arriving cold from an AI answer and the assistant itself the parent context a deep URL otherwise lacks.

suggested_action.summary: Add BreadcrumbList JSON-LD alongside visible breadcrumb navigation.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Emit BreadcrumbList JSON-LD listing each ancestor with position, name and item URL, and render the same trail visibly at the top of the page.

proactive_recommendations.title: Consider publishing llms.txt, with realistic expectations
proactive_recommendations.rationale: No /llms.txt is published. Be aware this is a low-evidence convention rather than an established standard: 2026 measurements find major AI crawlers almost never request the file, and Google has stated it has no effect on Search or AI Overviews. It costs very little to publish and may matter if uptake improves, but it should be treated as optionality -- not as a substitute for the structured data and third-party presence that demonstrably drive citation today.

suggested_action.summary: Optionally publish /llms.txt, after the higher-leverage items above.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: If you publish one, keep it to a short markdown index of your canonical product, docs, pricing and company pages, and keep it in sync with the site. Do not deprioritise schema work for it.
